What's new in Keeploop 0.27.6

  • A woken chat can open in iTerm or Warp instead of Terminal: pick the app under Settings > Monitors > When the chat is closed.
  • Agents with a route can watch every incoming call and voicemail (optionally missed calls only) and every new or changed note (optionally one folder).
  • Monitors on notifications, calls, notes, calendar and texts show their own fields in Settings > Monitors and can be saved. Before, a notifications monitor (such as one watching Slack or Teams) could not be saved, and an edit could drop part of its filter.
  • Add to ChatGPT in Settings > Remote access opens Keeploop in the ChatGPT plugin directory: choose Add there. With your own tunnel it still uses Create custom MCP server.
  • Codex delivery finds codex installed with nvm, so check_setup no longer says it cannot find the codex command.

What's new in Keeploop 0.27.5

  • Settings > Alerts and destinations has a Notifications table. For each kind of notification (monitor matches, agent resumed, wake asks, approvals, sending, promises, monitor changes, connection, account) choose a Mac banner and a sound; monitor matches, wake asks, approvals and promises can also go to your phone and Slack. The switch for messages to agent sessions moved into the table too. Sounds are off until you turn them on. Asks that block an action always show on the Mac.
  • One banner per monitor match. When the match's agent asks to resume, or runs in the background, that banner takes the match banner's place instead of adding a second one, and the phone gets the question only.
  • Monitors an agent made alert only when no agent picks up the match ("Only when no agent picks it up", on by default). An open session that already got the match no longer also shows a banner.
  • When an agent could not run, the banner always reads like "Claude Code not resumed: Invoices", with the reason below.
  • No more echo banners: no "Added to calendar" after you click Add, "Tracking" replaces "Promise found", and no "set a monitor" banner when an agent on this Mac made the change in the chat in front of you.
  • The older ntfy phone setting moves into the ntfy destination, so a match is never pushed to your phone twice.
  • Monitors can match everything for an agent that reads a route: match_all on the mail, Messages and Slack monitor tools (with routes only). For Slack it means every direct message, every group DM and every mention of you; texts cover phone numbers, email handles and short codes.
  • Mail monitors take a mailbox, such as INBOX. Gmail's inbox counts, though Gmail files that mail under All Mail.
  • A new monitor with routes starts with its Mac banner and phone push off, since an agent reads it and the source app shows its own banner. Phone destinations you add later stay off for it too. Turn them on per monitor in Settings > Monitors. Existing monitors keep their settings.

What's new in Keeploop 0.27.4

  • Monitors can now end on any date, or never. Settings > Monitors has an Ends control (On a date or Never) with quick Extend buttons, and the 30-day limit is gone. AI apps still set 24 hours unless you or they choose otherwise.
  • The details sheet of an ended monitor scrolls again.
  • A monitor set to never end stays that way: when ChatGPT renews it, Keeploop no longer adds an end date or moves an end date earlier.
  • Claude Code sessions that move to another git worktree of the same project no longer duplicate their monitors. When the old worktree folder is gone, its monitor moves to the new one; otherwise the AI app is told about the monitor in the other worktree and can move it. A monitor whose session is still open is never moved.
  • The monitor sheet's button now says Close, and rows no longer blur behind the buttons.

What's new in Keeploop 0.23.1

  • Keeploop's first public release.
  • Ask your AI about your Mac's Mail, Calendar, Messages, Notes, Contacts and Slack. Your data stays on your Mac.
  • Works with Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Cursor and other AI apps, on your Mac and on the web and phone.
  • Cards in ChatGPT and Claude show your inbox, today's schedule, free time and drafts.
  • Monitors tell you when a reply, a signature or an invite arrives.
  • Drafts and replies in your voice, and every send follows your rules: Blocked, Asked or Auto per account, label and contact.
  • You choose which accounts and sources each AI app can see.
  • One-time and sign-in codes are hidden from web and phone AI apps.
  • Optional health reports, off by default, and Report a problem.
